title: Navy Beans, canned, sodium added, drained and rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Navy beans are small, white, mildly sweet legumes that are often sold canned. In this product sodium has been added during processing, and the beans should be drained and rinsed before use.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “Navy” comes from the United States Navy, which used the beans as a staple ration.
Canned navy beans retain most of their nutrients, though sodium levels can be high.
They are a popular source of plant protein and fiber in vegetarian diets.
In the U.S. navy beans are commonly used in bean soups and baked bean dishes.
Rinsing canned beans can remove up to 40 % of the added sodium.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: A typical serving (about 130 g) provides roughly 8 g of plant‑based protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport, while folate supports DNA synthesis.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Navy beans cause a gradual rise in blood glucose, beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Contains magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals aid heart function and muscle contraction.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If not rinsed, the sodium can exceed daily recommendations, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people; introduce them gradually.

items.title: Phytic acid presence
items.content: Phytic acid may reduce mineral absorption; rinsing and cooking lower its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: After draining and rinsing, navy beans can be added to soups, salads, stews, chili, or used in vegetarian patties and casseroles. They also make a tasty side dish when tossed with olive oil, herbs, and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. Once opened, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3–4 days. Discard if an off‑odor or mold appears.
